cards.situation: At 4:30 pm on Friday, a relationship manager tells you she emailed a spreadsheet of 2,000 customers' names, IC numbers and loan balances to the wrong external address. The recipient has not replied. Her team leader suggests waiting until Monday to see whether the email bounces.

choices.text: Escalate at once under the breach procedure, start containment such as recall and contacting the recipient, and let the designated team assess immediate notification to BNM.
choices.outcome: MCIPD requires all staff to understand escalation, immediate containment, and immediate notification to BNM where a breach involves many customers or may cause significant harm. Waiting loses time that matters.

choices.text: Wait until Monday, as the team leader suggests, and escalate only if the recipient replies.
choices.outcome: Waiting over a weekend leaves the data exposed and delays any required notification. The size and sensitivity of the data call for immediate escalation.

choices.text: Ask the relationship manager to email the recipient asking him to delete the file, and close the matter there.
choices.outcome: Contacting the recipient may help containment, but handling it privately skips the bank's breach procedure, investigation and any notification duty.

cards.back: A high degree of awareness at all times of confidentiality, policies and the consequences of misuse (10.41).
Relevant training for all staff and regular reminders of their confidentiality obligations (10.43).
Specific induction training on customer information policies, plus notice of the actions for non-compliance (10.44, 10.45).
Mechanisms to gauge training effectiveness, for example an annual awareness survey (10.47, 10.48).
All staff understand escalation; relevant staff are trained on remedial action and on handling affected customers' queries (11.3, 11.31).
Providers must train their personnel at regular intervals on handling customer information (12.7).

cards.title: Who must train whom?
cards.prompt: Link each policy document to the training duty it contains.

pairs.right: Staff, representatives and agents trained on core values and desired conduct
Those dealing with vulnerable consumers trained to recognise, assess and respond
Sellers and marketers trained on product disclosure requirements
Complaints staff receive adequate and continuous training on procedures
All staff trained and reminded on confidentiality; induction for new staff

cards.question: Under the MCIPD policy document, how often must senior management ensure an independent review of the effectiveness of customer information controls?
options: At least once every two years
Only after a breach has occurred
Once, when the policy is first approved
cards.explanation: Paragraph 9.8 requires an independent review at least once in every two years. Paragraph 8.4 also requires annual written assurance from senior management to the Board.

cards.title: Ready for the regulator: what BNM will ask
cards.caption: A summary of the policy documents in this quest. Your bank's own conduct and compliance teams set the detailed evidence each function must keep.

items.label: Culture
items.left: Can you show FTFC in strategy, pay and Board papers?

items.label: Disclosure
items.left: Do products meet PTD rules at every stage?

items.label: Sales
items.left: Is advice suitable and free of Schedule 7 conduct?

items.label: Secrecy
items.left: Are controls, training and breach escalation working?

cards.title: Stage 5 takeaways
items: FSA section 133 bans disclosing customer information except to BNM, as non-identifying summaries or where already lawfully public; section 134 and Schedule 11 permit other disclosures on BNM's conditions.
Law enforcement requests must be specific, written on the prescribed forms and properly signed; never disclose on a phone call.
MCIPD 2025 requires high staff awareness, training and reminders, induction training, tests of training effectiveness and regular training by outsourced providers.
Escalate breaches at once; significant breaches go to BNM immediately.
BNM's 2019 action against CIMB Bank Berhad combined a RM6.4 million compound and a RM3.4 million penalty for disclosure and control failures.

cards.prompt: Which customer information do you handle every day, and where could it leave the bank without anyone noticing: a screen, a printout, a phone call, an email? What is one control you could tighten next week?

quiz.question: Who is bound by the secrecy duty in section 133 of the Financial Services Act?
options: Only the bank's directors, and not ordinary employees or agents
Only employees who work in branches and serve customers directly
Any person with access to customer information, including the bank and its directors, officers and agents
Only the compliance officer appointed to manage customer data
quiz.explanation: Section 133(1) applies to any person who has access to documents or information about a customer's affairs or account, expressly including the institution and its current and former directors, officers and agents.

quiz.question: A caller says he is a police officer and asks for a customer's statements by phone. What is the correct response?
options: Decline by phone and ask for a specific written request on the prescribed form, properly signed
Ask the customer's relationship manager whether to release them
Send the statements, because police requests are always permitted
Send only the last month's statement as a compromise
quiz.explanation: The MCIPD conditions for disclosures to investigating officers require a specific written request on the prescribed forms with the right signatory. A phone request meets none of them and may be social engineering.

quiz.question: Under section 134 of the FSA, a person who receives customer information through a permitted disclosure may:
options: Pass it on if the customer does not object within a week
Share it freely with their own business partners
Not disclose it to any other person
Publish it if it is more than a year old
quiz.explanation: Section 134(4) bars a recipient of permitted customer information from disclosing it to any other person, and breaching that is an offence under section 134(7).

quiz.question: What must a bank include in its programme for new staff under paragraph 10.44 of the MCIPD policy document?
options: A test on the bank's annual financial statements
A signed promise to report colleagues' personal finances
Specific training on policies and procedures for protecting customer information
Training only for those who will work in the data centre
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.44 requires specific induction training on customer information policies, and 10.45 requires telling new staff about the possible actions for non-compliance. It applies to all new staff.

quiz.question: Which mechanism does the MCIPD policy document give as an example of gauging the effectiveness of confidentiality training?
options: Checking that every employee has read the FSA
Counting how many emails each employee sends
Asking customers to rate staff on social media
An annual awareness survey of staff understanding
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.47 requires mechanisms to gauge training effectiveness, and guidance in 10.48 suggests an annual awareness survey on protecting customer information and reporting breaches.

quiz.question: When must a bank notify BNM of a customer information breach under paragraph 11.8 of the MCIPD policy document?
options: Within 30 days, but only if a customer has complained about it
At the next scheduled supervisory meeting with BNM
Immediately, if it poses reputational risk, may cause significant harm or affects many customers
Never, because breaches are handled entirely in-house
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.8 requires immediate notification on becoming aware of a breach that poses reputational or public-confidence risk, causes or may cause significant harm, or involves a large number of customers.

quiz.question: In BNM's enforcement action published as notice 02/2019, what did BNM impose on CIMB Bank Berhad?
options: A RM3.4 million administrative monetary penalty and a RM6.4 million compound
A licence suspension for six months and a public reprimand
A warning letter only, because the bank reported the incidents
A RM10 million fine imposed by the High Court after trial
quiz.explanation: The notice records an administrative monetary penalty of RM3.4 million for breaching customer information standards and a RM6.4 million compound for unauthorised disclosure offences under section 133(1).

quiz.question: What did BNM note as mitigating factors in the CIMB Bank Berhad customer information case?
options: The small number of customers affected by the incidents
The bank's agreement to close the branches involved
Voluntary reporting of the incidents and immediate remedial steps
The fact that the information was already public online
quiz.explanation: BNM said the amounts reflected aggravating and mitigating factors, including voluntary reporting of the incidents to BNM and the immediate remedial steps taken to strengthen controls.

quiz.question: What does the MCIPD policy document require of outsourced service providers that handle customer information?
options: They need only sign a confidentiality clause once
They are exempt because the bank remains responsible
They must be located inside the bank's head office
They must train their personnel regularly on handling customer information
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 12.7 requires the bank to ensure the provider trains its personnel at regular intervals and reviews that training. The bank must also review providers at least once every two years under 12.9.

quiz.question: A contractor in the call centre photographs a screen showing customer details. Which MCIPD measure targets this risk most directly?
options: Disclosing commission as a percentage before advice
Deterrent controls such as restricting personal devices in high-risk areas
Publishing complaint turnaround times on the website
Giving the customer a Product Disclosure Sheet in advance
quiz.explanation: Paragraphs 10.20 and 10.21 require deterrents to unauthorised disclosure, naming photographs of screens or documents and suggesting restrictions on personal devices in high-risk areas such as call centres.

regulators: Financial Markets Ombudsman Service (FMOS), the approved financial ombudsman scheme
Malaysia Competition Commission (referrals under FSA section 124(5))

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Sets the seven fair treatment outcomes and the charter duty, and requires staff, representatives and agents to be trained on core values and desired conduct, ideally role by role across the product life cycle.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Fair terms, training and supervision against misleading sales, no undue pressure, suitability, commission disclosure, adviser competence and complaints redress.

references.title: Policy Document on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers
references.note: Vulnerable consumer requirements, including training to recognise, assess and respond to their needs, applied from 1 April 2025.

references.title: Financial Services Act 2013 (Act 758)
references.note: BNM may set business conduct standards, including on suitability and affordability; banks must not engage in the six prohibited practices in Schedule 7.

references.title: Financial Services Act 2013 (Act 758)
references.note: Ombudsman scheme membership and compliance with awards; secrecy of customer information and the permitted disclosures route.

references.title: Policy Document on Product Transparency and Disclosure
references.note: Disclosure principles and stages, digital disclosure, marketing consent, advertising, language and PDS rules; sellers and intermediaries must be trained on disclosure requirements.

references.title: Policy Document on Prohibited Business Conduct
references.note: Guidance and examples for each Schedule 7 practice, and the factors BNM considers; banks are responsible for agents and service providers.

references.title: Policy Document on Complaints Handling
references.note: Complaint definition, empowered and continuously trained complaints staff, turnaround times, written decisions and referral to FMOS or BNMLINK (referral rules from 28 March 2025).

references.title: Policy Document on Management of Customer Information and Permitted Disclosures
references.note: Staff awareness, training and reminders, induction training, training effectiveness checks, breach escalation and notification, provider training and permitted disclosure conditions.

references.title: Deputy Governor's Speech at the Launch of the Financial Markets Ombudsman Service
references.note: FMOS formed by merging the Ombudsman for Financial Services and SIDREC, with a RM250,000 award limit for eligible disputes; gives industry complaint statistics.

references.title: Enforcement Action Publication Notice 02/2019: CIMB Bank Berhad and CIMB Islamic Bank Berhad
references.note: Administrative monetary penalty of RM3.4 million and compound of RM6.4 million on CIMB Bank Berhad for customer information standards breaches and unauthorised disclosure in 2018.

bank.question: A new digital bank asks whether the FTFC policy document applies to it before it has many customers. What is the best answer?
options: No. Digital banks follow only the Product Transparency and Disclosure document
Yes. It applies to licensed banks, and its standards bind the bank from the start of operations
Only its guidance applies, because new banks are exempt from the standards
No. It applies only once the bank has served customers for three full years
bank.explanation: The FTFC policy document applies to licensed banks, and BNM's conduct documents name digital banks among licensed banks. Nothing exempts new or digital banks from the S standards.

bank.question: A Board paper proposes measuring conduct success solely by the number of complaints received. Which FTFC expectation does this miss most clearly?
options: Monitoring FTFC outcomes across the product life cycle and fixing them where they are not met
Referring every complaint to the ombudsman before closing it
Asking BNM to approve each new marketing campaign in advance
Publishing the full remuneration policy for every sales employee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.3(i) makes senior management monitor FTFC outcomes and take corrective action. Complaint counts alone miss silent harm, such as unsuitable sales that customers never question.

bank.question: Which combination of facts best describes the 2024 FTFC policy document?
options: Issued 31 October 2025, replaced the 2023 version, and covers customer information protection
Issued 28 March 2025, replaced the 2009 guidelines, and applies in full from 1 April 2026
Issued 2 December 2024, replaced the 2013 guidelines, and phased in digital rules from 2026
Issued 27 March 2024, replaced the 2019 version, and deferred the vulnerable consumer rules to 1 April 2025
bank.explanation: The other options describe, in turn, the Product Transparency and Disclosure, Complaints Handling and Customer Information policy documents.

bank.question: A bank's sales staff earn 85% of their pay from variable incentives tied to sales volume. A supervisor finds no conduct indicators in their KPIs. Which pair of FTFC requirements is engaged?
options: Remuneration aligned with FTFC outcomes and a balanced ratio of fixed to variable pay
Customer consent for marketing and withdrawal within seven calendar days
Product disclosure in two languages and readability testing of contracts
Complaint acknowledgement by the next working day and progress updates
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 10.10 and 10.11 require remuneration aligned with FTFC, balanced fixed and variable components, and sufficient weight on qualitative criteria. The other pairs belong to other topics.

bank.question: Which example best shows a bank meeting FTFC Outcome 4?
options: A banker who signs the form on the customer's behalf to save time
A banker who explains a card's fees carefully and checks the customer has understood before applying
A banker who leaves the customer to read the full contract alone at home
A banker who closes the sale quickly so the customer does not have to wait
bank.explanation: Outcome 4 is that staff, representatives and agents exercise due care, skill and diligence. Careful explanation and a check of understanding show that; speed or shortcuts do not.

bank.question: An internal audit finds that branch staff received FTFC training, but contact-centre agents employed through a staffing agency did not. What is the best assessment?
options: A gap only if the agents also sell investment products to customers
No gap: contract workers supplied by an agency are outside FTFC entirely
A gap: the training duty covers staff, representatives and agents whose conduct affects customer outcomes
No gap: the staffing agency is solely responsible for training its own workers
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.6 covers staff, representatives and agents, and the FTFC definition of staff includes temporary or contract staff whose conduct affects outcomes. Contact-centre agents clearly affect outcomes.

bank.question: Which statement about S and G paragraphs is accurate?
options: S and G carry exactly the same weight, so the labels are only for layout
S paragraphs apply to insurers only, and G paragraphs apply to banks
Non-compliance with S paragraphs may result in enforcement action; G paragraphs are encouraged guidance
Non-compliance with G paragraphs is always a criminal offence under the FSA
bank.explanation: Each BNM policy document defines S as standards that must be complied with, where breach may lead to enforcement, and G as guidance and recommendations the bank is encouraged to adopt.

bank.question: Senior management wants FTFC training that BNM would see as well designed. Which design best matches paragraph 10.7?
options: Separate modules for sellers, product designers and collections staff showing FTFC at each life cycle stage
A single annual quiz on the FSA's section numbers, identical for every employee
A video of the CEO's speech on customer centricity, watched once at induction
A legal seminar for the Board only, since staff follow the Board's direction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.7 says training should be role-specific and address how the FTFC principles apply at the different stages of the product life cycle, as well as core values and desired behaviour.

bank.question: Under the FTFC policy document, what is 'conduct risk'?
options: The risk that the bank's business conduct leads to poor consumer outcomes and harms the bank's reputation or finances
The risk that customers break their contracts and fail to repay their loans on time
The risk that staff misconduct outside work damages their personal reputation
The risk that BNM changes its policy documents without giving advance notice
bank.explanation: FTFC defines conduct risk as risk from the bank's business conduct and practices that could cause poor consumer outcomes and reputational or financial impact. Paragraph 1.2 wants it inside the bank's risk management framework.

bank.question: A bank's mobile app shows the personal loan PDS beside a flashing banner for a holiday lucky draw. Which PTD requirement is breached?
options: Lucky draws may only be advertised to existing deposit customers
No promotional information may appear on the same page as the PDS on a digital channel
The PDS may only be shown after the loan has been disbursed
The PDS must be printed and posted before any app journey starts
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.7 requires the PDS to be displayed prominently on digital channels with no promotional information on the same page, so customers are not distracted from it.

bank.question: Your bank moves existing branch customers from paper statements to e-statements only. Under paragraph 11.18 of the PTD policy document, what must it do?
options: Switch everyone at once, since digital statements are always cheaper for customers
Obtain BNM's written approval for each customer before switching to e-statements
Consider their profile and give at least seven calendar days' written notice, including any fee for paper copies
Give at least 30 calendar days' notice and offer paper copies free for life
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.18 requires considering the customers' profile, at least seven calendar days' prior written notice, an explanation of the benefits to allow opting in, and clear disclosure of fees for physical copies.

bank.question: A brochure illustrates projected returns on an investment product using an assumed 12% annual growth that the product has never achieved. Which PTD rule applies most directly?
options: Projections are fine if the brochure is printed in both Bahasa Melayu and English
Avoid unrealistic assumptions, and label projections clearly as predictive and dependent on assumptions
Projections are fine if the customer signs to confirm reading the brochure
Projections are banned in all bank material regardless of how they are presented
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.4.4 bars hypothetical or unrealistic assumptions likely to mislead and requires a prominent statement that projections are predictive and depend on assumptions. Projections are not banned outright.

bank.question: A customer consents to the bank sharing her details with a partner insurer for marketing. Which form of consent is valid under paragraph 12.2 of the PTD policy document?
options: Consent assumed because she did not reply to an email about sharing
A standalone, unticked opt-in naming the insurer, the purpose and the data to be shared
A pre-ticked box that the customer could have unticked if she wished
A clause in the loan terms saying data may be shared with 'selected partners'
bank.explanation: Consent must be specific, voluntary, explicit and deliberate, and revocable. A vague clause, a pre-ticked box and silence all fail; the MCIPD guidance also says failure to opt out is not valid consent.

bank.question: For a complex product, what extra step does paragraph 16.8 of the PTD policy document give as an example to confirm customers understand the key terms and risks?
options: Sending a second copy of the full contract a year after the sale
Requiring customers to pass a written examination before purchase
Asking customers to sign a statement that they will not complain later
Calling customers after the sale to confirm they know the key terms and risks
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16.8 applies a risk-based approach to guiding customers through the PDS and, for complex products, requires additional steps such as post-sale calls to confirm awareness of key terms and risks.

bank.question: A unit trust advertisement shows a five-year chart of strong past returns with no comment. What must it also include under the PTD key disclosure principles?
options: A warning that past performance is not indicative of future performance
A guarantee that losses will be refunded by the bank
The fund manager's personal salary for the latest year
A list of all customers who have bought the fund before
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.5.1(d) requires a warning, wherever past performance is shown, that it does not indicate future performance. A refund guarantee would itself be misleading if not genuinely provided.

bank.question: An intermediary appointed by the bank sells a loan without giving the customer the PDS. Who is accountable under paragraph 17.1 of the PTD policy document?
options: Only the intermediary, because it made the sale independently
The bank, which must also act against the intermediary for the failure
Only the customer, who should have asked for the PDS
Nobody, because intermediaries are outside the PTD document
bank.explanation: Paragraph 17.1 requires the bank to ensure intermediaries comply and to act against those who fail to disclose, while the bank remains fully accountable for the failure.

bank.question: A contract term lets the bank keep all instalments already paid if the customer misses a single payment, with no limit. Which FTFC test is most relevant?
options: Whether the term creates a significant imbalance in the bank's favour to the customer's detriment
Whether the customer received the contract within seven days
Whether the term is printed in a font at least as large as the rest
Whether a competitor bank uses a similar term in its contracts
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.4 treats a standard-contract term as unfair if it tends to create a significant imbalance in rights and obligations against the consumer. Font size or industry practice does not make an unfair term fair.

bank.question: Which statement about the phased start of the PTD policy document is correct?
options: Every requirement started on 1 April 2026, when Complaints Handling also began
The digital disclosure section applied from issuance on 2 December 2024
The digital disclosure section applied from 1 January 2026, and PDS rules reached existing products then too
The PDS rules apply only to products launched after 1 January 2027
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4.1 brings paragraph 11 into force on 1 January 2026, paragraph 12 on 1 July 2025, and the PDS paragraphs on 1 July 2025 for new and 1 January 2026 for existing products.

bank.question: A banker tells a customer that a dual currency investment 'works just like a fixed deposit, only with better returns'. The product is not principal protected. Which prohibited practice is this?
options: Demanding payment for an unsolicited product or service
Coercing the customer into buying a second product
Misleading conduct, such as presenting a non-principal-protected product as a deposit
Colluding with other banks to fix the product's terms
bank.explanation: BNM's guidance gives claiming a non-principal-protected product is a deposit, and comparing such returns with deposits without explaining the risk of loss, as misleading conduct under Schedule 7.

bank.question: A bank automatically enrols all cardholders in a paid travel insurance add-on, charging them unless they phone to opt out. What does BNM's guidance say?
options: It is a pricing matter for the Competition Commission rather than BNM
It is acceptable because customers can cancel by phone at any time
It is acceptable if the charge is shown clearly on the monthly statement
It is demanding payment for an unsolicited product, which Schedule 7 prohibits
bank.explanation: BNM's guidance lists demanding payment under automatic enrolment schemes, where consumers are signed up without consent and deemed to accept unless they decline, as a breach of paragraph 4 of Schedule 7.

bank.question: A bank offers home loan customers a discount if they also open a current account, but still sells both products separately at normal prices. How does BNM's guidance treat this?
options: Always prohibited, because any bundle is a form of coercion
Permissible only if BNM approves each bundle in writing
Prohibited unless the current account has no fees at all
Generally permissible, because the customer can buy each product separately
bank.explanation: The guidance says a combination is not prohibited where the customer can buy the products separately or sees the value of the bundle, provided unbundled prices do not create a barrier.

bank.question: Under FTFC paragraph 14.9, what must staff give the customer after assessing suitability?
options: Information only on the product the customer first asked about
Information only on the product that earns the highest commission
Information on all the products assessed as suitable, so the customer knows the choices
Information on every product the bank sells, suitable or not
bank.explanation: Paragraph 14.9 requires information on all products assessed as suitable so the consumer is adequately informed of the choices. Steering to the highest-commission product would also breach 14.14.

bank.question: A banker is about to recommend a product where the customer's capital could be lost. What must happen first under FTFC paragraph 14.10?
options: Take reasonable steps to make sure the customer understands that risk before advising
Obtain a waiver excluding the bank's liability for poor advice
Check that the product has made a profit in each of the last three years
Confirm that the customer's family has agreed to the purchase
bank.explanation: Paragraph 14.10 requires reasonable steps so the customer understands the risk of capital loss before advice. Liability waivers are listed as poor practice and paragraph 13.4 bars excluding liability.

bank.question: A customer earning RM3,500 a month already spends most of it on existing debt. A banker offers him a large unsecured personal loan with a fast approval bonus. What does FTFC treat this as?
options: A predatory practice: enticing a highly indebted consumer to take on new unsecured debt
Acceptable if the loan is approved by an automated credit model
Acceptable if the customer confirms he understands the interest rate
Good service, because quick approval meets the customer's needs
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16.10(a) gives enticing highly indebted consumers with low savings into new loans, especially unsecured loans, as a predatory example. Understanding the rate does not make the loan affordable.

bank.question: A bank introduces a machine learning credit score that rejects far more applicants from some districts with no clear link to credit risk. Which FTFC paragraph is most relevant?
options: 15.10, requiring customers to be told about the ombudsman scheme
14.12, requiring commission to be disclosed as a percentage before advice
9.1, requiring the Treat Customers Fairly Charter on the website
16.12, requiring due care with AI and machine learning in credit assessment to avoid unfair discrimination
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16.12 requires due care when using AI and machine learning in credit assessments to avoid unfair discrimination and excessive pricing. Paragraph 13.8 also bars less favourable treatment on arbitrary factors.

bank.question: Under FSA section 123(2), BNM's conduct standards may cover which of the following?
options: The salary scale for the bank's directors
The bank's capital adequacy ratio and liquidity buffers
Assessments of the suitability and affordability of products offered to consumers
The bank's choice of external auditor each year
bank.explanation: Section 123(2)(d) lists recommendations and advice, including assessments of suitability and affordability. The section is about business conduct with consumers, not capital, auditors or director pay.

bank.question: A telemarketer calls the same customer daily for two weeks after she has said she is not interested. Which statement is correct?
options: It is allowed because telemarketing is outside BNM's conduct rules
It is allowed if the telemarketer is an outsourced agent, not bank staff
It is only a problem if the calls happen after 9 pm
Repeated solicitation after a stated lack of interest is an example of undue pressure under Schedule 7
bank.explanation: BNM's guidance gives repeated solicitations to a consumer who has said she is not interested as an example of undue pressure, and banks answer for agents and outsourced providers acting for them.

bank.question: A frontline officer notices that a customer seems confused, keeps asking the same question and is accompanied by a relative who answers for him. What does FTFC expect?
options: Process the transaction quickly to avoid embarrassing the customer
Recognise possible vulnerability, engage sensitively, adapt the service and escalate if needed
Refuse to serve the customer until a doctor's letter is produced
Deal only with the relative from now on, since he speaks for the customer
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 16.14 to 16.17 expect staff to be proactive, recognise and respond to vulnerability and escalate when appropriate. Demanding medical proof or bypassing the customer would be unfair.

bank.question: Which of these does FTFC guidance give as an example of good practice in training staff on vulnerable consumers?
options: A target for the number of vulnerable consumers sold credit cards
A rule that only senior managers may serve vulnerable consumers
'How to' guides by category of vulnerable consumer for frontline staff to use
A list of customers to avoid because they are likely to complain
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16.16 suggests internal programmes on signs of vulnerability, training on confidentiality and compassion, knowledge-sharing sessions and 'how to' guides for frontline staff.

bank.question: A customer's husband, the family's main earner, has died, and she cannot meet the home loan instalments. What does FTFC require of the bank?
options: A referral to the ombudsman scheme before the bank considers any solution
Easy-to-find information on getting help, and processes flexible enough to tailor solutions to her circumstances
A requirement that she repays the arrears before any discussion of options
Immediate foreclosure, because the contract terms must be applied strictly
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 16.21 to 16.23 require flexibility for staff, adaptable customer service processes and accessible information on assistance after sudden life events, with early engagement encouraged.

bank.question: Which complaint falls outside the turnaround times in the Complaints Handling policy document?
options: A complaint about an incorrect late payment charge
A complaint about a delayed loan disbursement
A complaint about a rude branch officer
A complaint about an unauthorised e-banking transaction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.2 says the turnaround times do not apply to complaints about unauthorised e-banking transactions, which follow BNM's separate requirements on fair treatment of victims of unauthorised transactions.

bank.question: A complex complaint was received on day 1. The bank has said nothing more by day 18 and expects to decide on day 20. Which requirement has it breached?
options: Senior management sign-off on every complex case by day 15
Referral to FMOS once a complaint passes 15 working days
Written acknowledgement within 20 working days of receipt
Progress updates at least once every 10 working days on complex cases
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.12 requires progress updates at least every 10 working days while a complex case is pending. The other requirements do not exist in this form.

bank.question: Which governance feature does the Complaints Handling policy document require to give an independent and impartial approach?
options: A complaints team that reports to sales so that revenue impact is known
A dedicated complaints handling function that tracks complaints and reviews resolution processes
A rule that branch managers resolve complaints about their own branches
An outsourced call centre that decides all complaints without bank input
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.3 requires a dedicated complaints handling function to ensure an independent and impartial approach, monitor the central platform and review processes for fair outcomes.

bank.question: Under paragraph 10.3 of the Complaints Handling policy document, what must appear on a bank's website?
options: A form that must be printed, signed and posted to lodge a complaint
The names and phone numbers of the bank's directors
A searchable list of every complaint received in the last three years
A 'Contact Us' tab at the top of the homepage that reaches the customer service page in one click
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.3 requires a prominent 'Contact Us' tab at the top of the homepage leading within one click to a customer service page with key information for lodging a complaint.

bank.question: An eligible complainant's dispute with the bank is within FMOS's jurisdiction. The bank's final decision goes against her. What must the bank do?
options: Refer her to the Financial Markets Ombudsman Service as a redress avenue
Tell her that only the civil courts can now help her
Tell her the decision is final and cannot be challenged
Refer her to BNMLINK, which decides banking disputes
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.3 requires referral to FMOS for eligible complainants whose disputes are within its jurisdiction. BNMLINK is the route under 12.4 only when FMOS cannot take the case.

bank.question: Under FSA section 126, what must a bank that is a member of an approved financial ombudsman scheme do?
options: Provide documents or information the scheme needs and comply with any award it grants
Approve each ombudsman appointment before the scheme can act
Pay each complainant's legal fees before the scheme hears a case
Refer all its complaints to the scheme before investigating them
bank.explanation: Section 126(4) requires member financial service providers to provide documents or information for dispute resolution and to comply with awards, including directions to take steps in a dispute.

bank.question: A customer's daughter, who is not authorised on the account, asks a branch officer for her mother's balance. Her mother is in hospital. What should the officer do?
options: Give the balance, because she is a close family member and it is urgent
Decline unless a valid permission or legal authority under Schedule 11 applies, and explain the options
Give the balance if the daughter shows her own identity card
Give the balance verbally, since secrecy covers written disclosure only
bank.explanation: Section 133 bars disclosure to another person unless an exception or a Schedule 11 permitted disclosure applies, such as written permission from the customer or a legal personal representative where the customer is incapacitated.

bank.question: Which statement about section 133(3) of the FSA is correct?
options: Only the original discloser commits an offence, never the recipient
Leaked information becomes public once it has been shared twice
A person who knows information was disclosed unlawfully must not disclose it further
A person who receives leaked information may use it if he paid for it
bank.explanation: Section 133(3) bars anyone holding information that, to their knowledge, was disclosed in breach of 133(1) from disclosing it to anyone else, and section 133(4) makes this an offence.

bank.question: Which pair of MCIPD requirements apply to the Board and senior management?
options: Senior management sign-off on each new account and annual training of BNM staff
Board tone from the top and annual written assurance, plus an independent review at least every two years
Board review of all staff emails and a review of outsourced providers every five years
Board approval of each disclosure to the police and monthly breach reports to customers
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.1 sets the Board's tone from the top, 8.4 requires annual written assurance from senior management, and 9.8 requires an independent review at least once every two years.

bank.question: After a staff member deliberately leaked customer data, the bank decides not to take disciplinary action. What does the MCIPD policy document require?
options: Publication of the staff member's name on the bank's website
Automatic referral of the staff member to the ombudsman scheme
Nothing, because disciplinary matters are outside BNM's interest
Proper documentation of the reasons, approved at the appropriate senior level
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 10.49 and 10.50 require investigation and action that deters recurrence; where no action is taken, the reasons must be properly documented and approved by senior management.

bank.question: Which training duty applies to staff when a customer information breach occurs?
options: Only IT staff need training, as breaches are technical events
Staff must be trained to deny that any breach occurred until BNM confirms it
Relevant staff must be trained to handle affected customers' queries and advise on protective steps
Staff must be trained to refer all affected customers to the police
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.31 requires staff to be trained to handle queries from affected customers and help them with protective measures, and 11.3 requires all staff to understand escalation procedures.

bank.question: BNM's notice on CIMB Bank Berhad (P.N. 02/2019) involved both a compound and an administrative monetary penalty. Why two different sanctions?
options: The compound was paid by staff personally; the penalty was paid by the bank
The compound was for late reporting; the penalty was for a misleading advertisement
The compound was for the conventional bank; the penalty was for a payment operator
The compound related to unauthorised disclosure offences; the penalty to breaching customer information standards
bank.explanation: The notice shows a RM6.4 million compound for offences under section 133(1) and a RM3.4 million penalty under section 234 of the FSA for breaching the standards in the customer information policy document.

bank.question: A bank is preparing for a BNM conduct review. Which evidence best shows that its FTFC training duty under paragraph 10.6 is met?
options: A statement from the CEO that all staff understand fair treatment
A single attendance sheet from a launch event held five years ago
Role-specific training records linked to outcome monitoring and corrective action
Marketing material describing the bank as customer-focused
bank.explanation: Supervisors look for evidence that training reached staff, representatives and agents, fitted their roles and influenced outcomes. Old attendance lists or slogans do not show that.

bank.question: Which description best matches the training duties in the policy documents covered by this quest?
options: FTFC and MCIPD cover all staff, while PTD focuses on sellers and Complaints Handling on complaints staff
Every document requires the same annual course for every employee
Only the FTFC policy document contains any training duty for bank staff
Training duties apply to the Board only, which then briefs staff
bank.explanation: FTFC 10.6 covers staff, representatives and agents; MCIPD 10.43 covers all staff; PTD 8.6 targets sellers and marketers; Complaints Handling 9.4 targets complaints staff; FTFC 16.15 targets those serving vulnerable consumers.

bank.question: Paragraph 12.7 of the MCIPD policy document concerns outsourced service providers handling customer information. What does it require of their training?
options: They must train their personnel at regular intervals and review that training's adequacy and effectiveness
They need no training if the contract includes a confidentiality clause
They must use the bank's own trainers for every session they run
They must send their personnel to BNM for certification every year
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.7 requires the bank to ensure the provider trains its personnel regularly and reviews the training programme. Guidance in 12.8 adds that the bank may also train the provider's staff.
